explanation:
CONFORMANCE: PASS for the affected source-selection/query-path cluster against the approved F23 amendment and the main module ledger/S4 plan; this is a structural source review, not a claim that every S4 behavioral, platform, census or qualification gate passes. The independent production reconstruction was completed before reading the approved design; comparison subsequently used design.md:155–180,282–326 and plan.md:285–307, without reading review-decisions.md or treating Main's reported validation results as structural proof.

EXPLICIT CONFORMANCE CHECKS
1. Approved policy owner — PASS. design.md:298,308 selects the existing private ModuleResolver seam. Production module_resolver.rs:63–71,121–123 defines crate-private SourcePathIdentity and the trait operation; the Rust implementation returns Logical (267–269), CSharp returns Physical (362–364), and the existing exhaustive static registry dispatches both (226–231). No new policy registry, public discovery operation, extraction-policy interface, allocation-bearing factory, database operation or process invocation was introduced for source identity.
2. Neutral source-selection caller — PASS. design.md:309 expressly leaves shared candidate selection, canonicalization and diagnostics in indexing.rs. discover_files (1200–1279) calls get_module_resolver(language).source_path_identity(), matches Logical/Physical rather than Rust/CSharp, and owns the neutral execution mechanics. This is approved responsibility, not forbidden policy duplication. My reconstruction's warning that future normalization mechanics could drift is a maintenance observation only; it is not a present ledger mismatch.
3. Neutral query normalization — PASS. design.md:310 expressly leaves lexical normalization/query-path conversion in lib.rs. relative_path (294–345) obtains the same resolver-declared identity, preserves logical in-workspace spelling, canonicalizes physical candidates against workspace_root and retains lexical fallback for unavailable paths. Its operation selection is policy consumption, not another language rule. Public query entry points remain unchanged.
4. Existing adapters and resolver semantics — PASS. Rust/CSharp implementations remain substantive existing adapters. Rust continues using resolver::resolve_module_path and ordered qualified splits; CSharp continues namespace-based one-to-many resolution and its existing glob policy. resolve.rs:352–388 explicitly consumes GlobPolicy and467–490 honors first-indexed-candidate claiming. F23 does not authorize changing these semantics, and no identity-related rerouting/drop was observed.
5. Immutable context — PASS. main ledger design.md:179 and S4 plan.md:295 authorize precomputed snapshot/CrateInfo context. ModuleContext.discovery is a borrowed immutable DiscoverySnapshot (module_resolver.rs:53–60); Rust uses its crates. My earlier note that this is a broader dependency than the currently consumed data is not a mismatch: this representation is explicitly approved. No evaluator or SQL code moved into ModuleResolver.
6. Freshness and unused-import callers — PASS. design.md:311 and main ledger:180 retain existing query behavior and forbid discovery execution/new identity policy there. needs_update/get_stale_files call the shared selector with indexed paths (reindex.rs:73–78,123–128); lookup_key/classify_changed_files call relative_path. find_unused_imports uses the same selector then keeps its existing Rust-only analysis (unused_imports.rs:92–107,175–183). Filtering for the already Rust-only algorithm is not a duplicate source-identity rule. No project evaluation is invoked by these query paths.
7. Publication-versus-query direction — PASS within the inspected scope. index_in_revision invokes discover_workspace once per index/rebuild invocation with owned discovery options and cache (indexing.rs:181–201); read-only construction instead loads the stored snapshot with the approved fresh/rebuild Cargo fallback (lib.rs:183–220). Evaluated membership is consumed as source candidates alongside walked/retained syntax, rather than being mistaken for the complete physical syntax inventory. This matches S4's distinction between syntax and evaluated participation and its prohibition on query-triggered evaluation.
8. Rust compatibility/C# containment separation — PASS by source structure. Rust logical candidates avoid physical canonicalization in discover_files and retain distinct aliases; C# candidates canonicalize, require workspace containment and deduplicate by canonical path (indexing.rs:1236–1272). External Rust targets are intentionally retained under design.md:313, not an outstanding security finding. External C# candidates produce source errors and do not reach parsing. F23 explicitly rejects repository-wide Rust symlink hardening.
9. Existing test surfaces — PASS by inspection of test structure, not execution. tests/symlink_boundary.rs asserts retained external logical Rust paths and distinct alias identities; tests/concurrency_and_filesystem.rs's new canonical-alias and external-target tests are C#, as requested by F23; tests/msbuild_discovery.rs retains membership, untrusted source-only, replacement/failure and evaluated-only freshness fixtures. Direct SQL observations in msbuild_discovery.rs are intentional independent-oracle access under S4, not improper reach-through to private source-selection helpers. Native cases remain explicitly ignored unless the native runner opts in.
10. Ordering — No conformance mismatch found. The new seen set does not determine vector iteration order; discover_files preserves first encounter. Existing read_dir ordering and HashMap-derived freshness ordering remain nondeterministic, so no stronger deterministic-order guarantee is inferred. Resolver candidate ordering and unused-import final sorting remain explicit.

MISMATCHES
None established in the affected cluster. Original discovery/storage owner rows are unchanged by F23 and were not rejudged as if the amendment authorized moving them. I do not propose a new source-identity module or moving neutral normalization into the resolver: either would contradict the selected amendment's stated ownership.

ASSUMPTIONS AND BOUNDED OBSERVATIONS
• This PASS covers responsibility placement, actual interfaces, dependency direction and inspected caller/consumer structure. Exact cfg(test)-excluded production line counts and numeric growth caps require the existing census proof; no counting/oracle command was run in this review, so numeric cap compliance is not independently asserted.
• F23 identifies language/path-shape coverage but does not specify mixed-extension aliases. Existing source control flow chooses policy from the candidate spelling and then chooses parser language from the normalized result: Alias.cs→target.rs uses physical normalization then Rust parsing, while Alias.rs→Target.cs retains logical identity and Rust parsing. Unsupported normalized extensions are skipped. These consequences are recorded rather than silently assuming every alias preserves its extension; no explicit approved contract was found that makes them a conformance failure.
• Missing physical target lookup falls back lexically; a now-broken alias cannot reconstruct a historical canonical target. The inspected amendment does not require reverse alias-history storage, so this is not treated as a failure of missing-file query behavior.
• Retention operates on every indexed path rather than checking Physical alone (indexing.rs:1209–1213). The requirement mandates retained physical syntax but does not explicitly prohibit retaining logical syntax; no observable contradiction to the approved Rust compatibility baseline was established.
• Freshness queries answer source mtime/size availability against the persisted snapshot, not whether changed project inputs would reevaluate to different membership. The plan requires reevaluation/validation during index/reindex invocations, not during these read-only queries; no query-time evaluator was inferred or requested.
• Source-selection errors remain warnings plus caller-owned sinks; freshness and unused-import callers do not expose those sinks. This is the observed retained caller shape and not a new requirement to alter their public error interfaces.
• Reciprocal policy mutants, ordinary/native suites, doctests, strict clippy, CLI/SQL proof and resource/platform gates remain Main-owned evidence. I neither reran them nor used their reported success to bypass this comparison.
